etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English whan evere, whanne ever, whanne evere, whener, when ever; equivalent to when +‎ ever.

quote.citation: 1987 December 21, Richard Nixon, Letters to Trump, Winning Team Publishing, published 2023, →ISBN, →OCLC, page 10:
quote.text: I did not see the program, but Mrs. Nixon told me that you were great on the Donahue Show.As you can imagine, she is an expert on politics and she predicts that whenever you decide to run for office you will be a winner!

definitions.definition: At the (single) time that, no matter when.

quote.citation: 2024 January 24, Peter Plisner, “Rising to the University challenge”, in RAIL, number 1001, page 61:
quote.text: Working around an ancient monument has meant having an archaeologist on site whenever there were excavations.

definitions.definition: (interrogative) When ever: emphatic form of when.
